checks.title: Time range
checks.detail: We set the dashboard's time window to cover the incident.

checks.title: Key panel
checks.detail: We selected the ${var.field_label} that stood out, so every panel filtered to it.

checks.title: Records behind the chart
checks.detail: We opened the records behind the chart to confirm it.

answer.evidence: The selected ${var.field_label} and the records behind it connect ${truth.finding} to ${truth.scope}.

goals.title: Set the time window
goals.concept: Setting a time range separates the incident from everyday, background activity in every panel at once.
goals.narration: The report says the problem was first noticed at ${incident.noticed_clock} (${incident.noticed_ago}). Start the dashboard's time window a little before then. Every panel then covers that moment, without much older traffic.
goals.reasoning: A short time range keeps the incident in view. Older data from normal times would only confuse the comparison.
goals.evidence: The results refresh to the window you picked.

demonstration.narration: The problem was noticed at ${incident.noticed_clock}. I'll start the dashboard's window at ${incident.window_start_clock}, the five-minute mark before it. Every panel then covers that moment, without older traffic.
demonstration.evidence: Every panel now starts at ${incident.window_start_clock}, so the report at ${incident.noticed_clock} is in view. Next, read the panels for the ${var.field_label} that stands out.

drifts.note: You filtered the dashboard before setting its time window; this step is about choosing when to look.

hints: Too short a window misses the report entirely; a much longer one mixes older, normal traffic into every panel.
Click the date box above the panels. Type a start date and time, then “to now”. It applies to every panel at once.
Start the window at ${incident.window_start_clock}: type “${incident.window_start_typed} to now”. Show me can do it for you.

goals.title: Select the value that stands out
goals.concept: Clicking a chart value filters every panel to it, without editing the dashboard.
goals.narration: Find the panel that splits the incident by ${var.field_label}. Click the value that stands out, so every panel filters to it.
goals.reasoning: A total can hide which part is causing the change. The panel that splits it up shows that.
goals.evidence: Every panel now shows only the selected value.

demonstration.narration: I'll click the ${var.field_label} that stands out in its panel, so every other panel filters to the same value.
demonstration.reasoning: A total can hide which part is causing a change. Clicking the value that stands out filters every panel to it, without editing the dashboard.
demonstration.evidence: Every panel now filters to ${var.value}, the ${var.field_label} that stood out. Check the records behind the chart before deciding what the pattern means.

drifts.note: You filtered to ${action.value}; check whether that is really the ${var.field_label} that stands out.
You selected ${action.value}; check whether that is really the ${var.field_label} that stands out.

hints: Look for the panel that splits the incident by ${var.field_label}; one value should stand apart.
Click its bar, or open its legend entry's menu and choose Filter for, to filter every panel to it.
Select ${var.value}; Show me can point it out.

goals.title: Check the records behind the chart
goals.concept: A chart is an aggregation: a summary of many records. The records behind it show what it really counted.
goals.narration: Open the records behind the panel, keeping its filter and time, and check that they show what the chart suggests.
goals.reasoning: This checks that the chart means what your conclusion will say.
goals.evidence: The records behind the chart hold the facts it counts.

demonstration.narration: I'll open the records behind the chart, with the same filter and time, to check what they show.
demonstration.reasoning: It's easy to misread a chart if you don't know its formula, buckets or filters. The records behind it show what it really counted.
demonstration.evidence: The highlighted fields on this record match the selected ${var.field_label}, so the chart's pattern is real. ${truth.conclusion}

hints: Check the chart against the records it counts.
Hover the panel and use Explore in Discover (or Inspect) to see them with the same filter and time.
Open the data behind the panel; Show me can do it for you.

goals.title: Submit a conclusion the dashboard backs up
goals.concept: Point to both the pattern on the chart and the records behind it.
goals.narration: Record the conclusion without editing or saving the dashboard.
goals.reasoning: Even without editing anything, leave a trail of evidence that someone else can follow.
goals.evidence: The answer points to the panel and the records behind it.
hints: Sum up what the evidence shows.
Use the coach's answer form: name what you found, its scope, and what the evidence shows.
Submit the finding, scope and conclusion; Show me shows the reference summary.
